# F20 and F21 fixed, and what F21 says about the thing this ticket is for

Ruud's call: fix both. Red 278 and green 279 are the round, and the red is worth
reading rather than summarising, because it reproduces the defect in the runner's own
words: with `scripts/rules.sh` back at its committed version and a violating
`packages/core/src/violation with space.ts` staged, the script printed

    ==> Biome on the staged files
    Checked 0 files in 231ms. No fixes applied.
        biome: ok in 0s

and exited 0. A hook that reports ok having read nothing is the exact failure
`harness/rules.py` is written around at length, one layer out in the shell, and it took
four reviews to find because every measurement this ticket ever took used paths without
spaces in them.

## F21, fixed properly rather than quoted

The list is no longer a string that the shell splits. `staged_paths` emits NUL-delimited
paths, `run_staged` reads them into three arrays with `read -r -d ''`, the extension
decides which array a path joins in a `case` rather than a regex over the whole set, and
each tool is handed `"${array[@]}"`. The `shellcheck disable=SC2086` comments are gone
with the splitting they excused, and so is `keep`, which existed only to filter the
flattened string.

Three tests hold it, and the first two are the cheap ones that would have caught it:
`test_the_staged_run_hands_each_tool_only_the_staged_paths` now asserts the quoted
array form; `test_the_staged_run_never_word_splits_its_path_list` asserts that no bare
`$code_paths`, `$module_paths` or `$all` survives and that the read is NUL-delimited;
and `StagedPathWithASpaceTest` runs the real script over a real staged violation whose
path has a space, and asserts exit 1 with the file named and no "Checked 0 files". That
last one runs against this repository, because `scripts/rules.sh` cds to its own root
and there is no second tree to point it at: it writes the violation, uses a throwaway
`GIT_INDEX_FILE` so the real staging area is untouched, and removes the file in
tearDown. It skips when `node_modules` is absent, as the hook itself does.

## F20, fixed, and honestly without a test

`Math.round(amountCents * 15) / 100` becomes `Math.round((amountCents * 15) / 100)` in
both functions of the knip fixture, so `commissionCents(1001)` is 150 rather than
150.15. No test covers it, and that is deliberate rather than an omission: the finding's
own rule candidate says no rule of this set can read the fixture tree, which is true by
design, and a test asserting a fixture's incidental arithmetic would be a test written
for the bookkeeping. What catches this class properly is SEEN-135's branded `Cents`,
where a number that is not integer cents cannot be assigned at all. The fixture still
fires: 23 of 23 rules refuse their own fixture after the change.

## What the next round does

The usual replay, and this time the production tree moved, so nothing from attempt 12
can be cited: `.harness-drafts/replay2.sh` for the five pairs, `.harness-drafts/round6.sh`
for the sixth, then the seventh round is this one, red 278 and green 279, which stays
citable because it is this attempt's own. Then the three measurements, the tdd record
with every count read out of its check, the status and the boxes, the figures, and the
regression and the coverage last.

Checks 253, 254 and 277 belong to this attempt and must not be re-taken: they measure a
directory this ticket does not touch.

## Where the ticket stands

Twenty-one findings over four reviews. Eighteen are closed, three are carried with their
reasons (F9, F10, F17) beside the rule four of the figure findings asked for. Not one
review has questioned the rule set itself, and the fourth went further than any of them:
it rebuilt the deleted provider boundary's replacement in a throwaway tree and watched it
catch a require, a dynamic import and a bare import; it compared every reformatted
TypeScript file before and after with whitespace normalised away and found no assertion
moved; and it opened all twenty-three citations. What the reviews have been finding is
the account of the work, four times a figure and once a shell quoting bug, and the last
of those is the only one that was in the deliverable.
